new_destinations.name: Tuatapere
new_destinations.why: Gateway town of the western Southland coast on the Southern Scenic Route (Wikipedia, Wikivoyage Southland), base for the Hump Ridge Track (a Great Walk since 2024) and the lakes and historic bridge around it. Roughly 123 km from Fiordland's centre, so outside Fiordland's 75% span (105 km); Hump Ridge and Clifden are already standalone spots. NOTE: Lake Monowai (about 95 km from Fiordland centre) is technically inside Fiordland's span but is reached from here, via Clifden.

spots.coordinates_source: Commons geotag of Lake-Hauroko-pier.jpg (jetty)
spots.bio: New Zealand's deepest lake at 462 m, reached by a gravel road from Tuatapere, set in a Fiordland valley with a jetty at the shore.

new_destinations.name: Glenorchy
new_destinations.why: Village at the head of Lake Wakatipu, about 45 km by road from Queenstown, with its own journey and base for the Routeburn, Greenstone-Caples and Rees-Dart tracks (Wikivoyage Glenorchy); Paradise, Diamond Lake and the Dart River valley around it give four or more spots. COVERAGE.md uses Glenorchy as a standalone spot, but with Paradise now qualifying as a spot of its own it clears the three-spot bar. Routeburn Track stays in Fiordland (fiordland-8). NOTE id collision: destination id 'glenorchy' = existing standalone spot id 'glenorchy', which must be removed (see existing_fixes); a visited flag on that spot would need migrating, or use destination id 'glenorchy-paradise' to avoid it.

new_destinations.name: Twizel
new_destinations.why: Mackenzie Country's largest town and the closest sizeable base to Aoraki / Mount Cook (Wikivoyage Twizel); 58 km from Aoraki's centre and 45 km from Lake Tekapo, so outside both spans (37.5 and 18.75 km). Holds the southern Mackenzie: Omarama's Clay Cliffs, Lake Ōhau, Lake Benmore and Lake Ruataniwha (Wikivoyage Twizel, Omarama). Lindis Pass sits inside Central Otago's span and is left there.
